svg.text: Presenter's side
Demo Console process: python console\server.py
Modules and helpers a job calls
Putting the console on the jump box (Deploy-JumpBox-Console.bat, safe to re-run)
Started by Start-Console.bat on the laptop, or by the ABW Demo Console desktop shortcut on the jump box. Either way the
operator's az login is checked first and the browser opens on the console. Closing the window stops it.
server.py: Starlette and uvicorn on 127.0.0.1 only (the
next free port if 8787 is busy). Serves the web UI and the
/api routes. Sets security headers, accepts only localhost
host names and refuses a POST that is not same-origin.
jobs.py (Manager): one button press is one job, in its own
thread, with plain-English events the browser polls.
Disruptive scenes never overlap each other or anything
that calls the gateway (the allow-list scene may run
beside an agent run); two agent runs never overlap;
read-only jobs always run.
catalog.py: the story. Scenes (Acts 1-7), beats,
plain-English allow and deny reasons, architecture cards,
portal links for 'Prove it's real' and the KQL pack.
personas.py: signs a persona in once with a device code
against abw-test-client, then asks for tokens silently, so a
job never prompts. Passwords stay in .secrets and reach
only the clipboard; TOTP seeds never leave it (the page
gets the 6-digit code).
azure_probe.py: read-only probes of Foundry, APIM, the
MCP servers, data, Monitor, Sentinel, Policy, Defender,
Entra and more. Each result is cached 120 s. Feeds the
Control Room and 'Prove it's real'.
agent_run.py: one Foundry agent turn in a child process,
one JSON event per line. Approval requests go to the
browser. Enters at the APIM /agents front door once it is
deployed, else direct; the legacy PoC agent always goes
direct.
e2e.py (Act 6): one request through twelve layers: Entra,
Conditional Access, guardrails, agent, gateway, MCP
server, data and five watchtowers. Boards live in memory
only; every row carries an evidence tag.
act7.py (Act 7): role matrix, FinOps, token budget, agent
path and front door. Its only change is the two APIM
named values for the front-door limits, always restored.
role_story.py and role_tabs.py: one tab per person plus
the Administrator, each with a positive and a negative
beat. A persona makes a real gateway call with their own
token; the Administrator runs the agents through the front
door.
Helpers and child processes: demo\mcpclient.py makes
gateway calls in process. Child processes:
scripts\kill-switch.ps1, scripts\client-allowlist.ps1,
demo\burst.py, demo\try-violations.py and demo\prove.py.
Presenter or operator. Signs in once with
their own az login, then presses the beat
buttons.
Browser at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ (the
default browser on the laptop, Edge on
the jump box). Plain JavaScript, no CDN.
Pages: Start, Acts 1-5, Act 6 boards, Act
7 roles and cost, Control Room,
Scoreboard. A strip lights up the layers a
job touches.
Credentials, local only. The operator's az
login cache gives silent tokens for ARM,
Graph, Log Analytics, Foundry and the
MCP APIs. .secrets\msal-test-<id>.json
holds one device-code sign-in per
persona (an MSAL cache: the refresh
token plus short-lived access tokens).
Proof evidence for the Scoreboard and
the replay rows. The laptop holds the raw
files; the jump box gets only a scrubbed
copy.
Private browser window for a persona's
device-code sign-in. Human step: the
person enters the code and completes
MFA.
Foundry project: the agents and their Responses API
(audience https://ai.azure.com)
API Management gateway: /research, /wall, /actions,
/vendor, /legacy and the /agents front door
Azure Resource Manager: resources, Azure Policy,
APIM named values, Cost Management, Defender
alerts
Log Analytics query API: the audit, gateway and App
Insights tables
Microsoft Graph: the directory and the sign-in log
Entra ID sign-in: the device-code flow for each persona
Stage (laptop): Deploy-JumpBox-Console.bat runs
scripts\jumpbox-console.ps1, which builds a
whitelist package: the console, the agent and demo
code, the policy XML, the KQL and Sentinel packs,
the generated infra JSON (resource names and ids,
no keys) and the scrubbed evidence. It scans the
package for secrets before anything is sent.
Start (laptop): starts the VM if it is stopped, then
reads the state of C:\abw on it with one Azure
run-command probe. Safe to re-run.
Tools (in the VM): installs Python, Azure CLI and
PowerShell 7 when missing. Each installer must
carry a valid signature.
Package (in the VM): receives the zip in base64
chunks, rebuilds it, checks its SHA-256 and copies
it to C:\abw. Never overwrites demo\evidence.
Venv (in the VM): creates C:\abw\.venv and installs
the requirements with the constraints file, only when
either file changed.
Launcher: desktop shortcuts for the console and
the Azure and Foundry portals. C:\abw\.secrets is
locked to SYSTEM and the local admin.
Verify: a throw-away console on port 8799 (health,
UI, catalog, scoreboard, policy, personas), private
DNS, an unauthenticated APIM call and a silent
sign-in check for each persona already on the VM.
Show day: Start-JumpBox.bat starts the VM and
copies its password. In the Azure portal: the VM,
Connect, Bastion. The first run also needs a
one-time az login with a device code as the
operator.
Run: the desktop shortcut starts
scripts\jumpbox-console-start.ps1, which starts the
console and opens Edge at http://127.0.0.1:8787/.
Closing the window stops it.
Never copied: .secrets by default, the legacy key,
raw evidence, the deck, the docs. Persona files
travel only with -IncludePersonaFiles.
Demo Console: components, targets and jump-box install
One local web app; tokens come from the operator's az login or a persona's own sign-in
Agents Behind the Wall - diagram 12 of 13 - generated by docs/diagrams/build_diagrams.py
Legend

Network, API gateway (APIM)

Observability

What the console calls
In the VM, each phase is one Azure run-command call (as SYSTEM, in Windows PowerShell 5.1) that returns one JSON line. The first failing phase stops the run, and every phase can be repeated.
What to notice
- No token, password or TOTP seed is printed or sent to the browser. Every token comes from the
operator's az login or a persona's own device-code sign-in. The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only and
refuses cross-origin POSTs.
- Every board row carries an evidence tag, so observed facts are never mixed up with replayed or
portal-only ones. The jump box holds only the scrubbed copy of the evidence.
- The Act 6 and Act 7 boards change nothing in Entra except 6.1's real failed sign-ins for one demo user
(at most five in ten minutes). Act 7 changes only the two front-door named values and restores them;
Reset demo restores the baseline: kill switch, allow-list, limits and the operator's roles.
Main flow (numbers on the arrows)
1. The presenter presses a beat button in the browser.
2. The browser sends POST /api/jobs to 127.0.0.1. The server refuses it unless it is
same-origin.
3. jobs.py starts the job in its own thread. Scripts and agent turns run as child processes.
4. The job runs the beat through a module: catalog, probe, e2e, act7, agent_run or a helper.
5. The module takes a token silently from the operator's az login, or from a persona's own
cache, and calls the target.
6. The job emits plain-English events. The browser polls GET /api/jobs/{id}, draws the cards
and lights the strip. Each row carries an evidence tag: live, probe, logs, graph, arm, replay
or portal (Act 7 adds rbac and design).
